Clean pass with three caveats. (1) Stata 80-character label cap: 5 of the 8 variable labels in the S1 .dta are truncated mid-phrase. Four of the eight items reproduce the Questionnaire for Assessing the Impact of the COVID-19 Pandemic on Older Adults (QAICPOA; Cawthon et al. 2020, J Gerontol A, doi:10.1093/gerona/glaa099, Table 1) verbatim -- concern = QAICPOA Q1 (complete in the label), difficulty_food/difficulty_medicine/routine_medical_difficult = Q12/Q13/Q14, whose surviving label wording is an exact character-for-character prefix of QAICPOA (50/45/50 characters respectively -- the 80-char figure is the RAW label length, which includes Stata's 'RECODE of qNN_x (' wrapper, so the usable match is shorter than the cap suggests) -- so those three ship the full QAICPOA wording. memory and difficulty_earning have no QAICPOA counterpart and ship the truncated label verbatim ('...during last mont', '...obtaining the e'); nothing was invented to complete them. (2) option_text is the value labels of the RECODEd binary variables ('No difficulty'/'Some difficulty' etc.), which is what IRW resp 0/1 actually encodes -- not the administered response options, which for the QAICPOA-derived items were None/some/much/unable or very difficult. (3) Administered in Bengali (paper: the English questionnaire was translated into Bengali and back-translated); no Bengali wording exists anywhere in the deposit (S1 Data .dta is the only supplementary file, all labels English), so the study's own English sits in the base fields under the translated_substitute fallback with language=Bengali and empty _translated columns. RETRY TEST: NO -- a determinate verdict was reached; the item and resp sets both gate clean and the only residual gap (2 truncated 80-char Stata labels) is a property of the sole deposited file, which an unchanged retry would re-download identically. Only a newly published questionnaire or a do-file from the authors would change it.
